name: Watercolor Studio
description: A quiet, beautiful place to paint with watercolors, one sheet of textured paper per session of the frame. Pigments are real watercolor pans: pick one, or add bits of several into the mixing well and they blend subtractively the way paint does (blue plus yellow makes green, complements make mud). A range of brushes (broad wash, round, flat, dry-brush, fine detail) lay translucent washes that pool, bleed and darken at their edges; layered strokes glaze over one another, and a clean-water Lift brush pulls pigment back out. Optional faint guide outlines (a pear, a teacup, a koi, a mountain lake…) sit beneath the paint for new painters to trace. Editors paint together in real time and undo their own strokes; the owner sets the title, paper, sheet shape and guide, and can clear the sheet; viewers and anonymous visitors watch read-only and can save the picture. The painting is files of the space, in its own folder under "Watercolor Studio/": painting.png, a picture anyone in the space can open, and strokes.json, the vector strokes the frame replays and keeps editing. No network.
